subject: gov.policy

subject: gov.legislate
name: Access to Information Bill
milestone: Final draft examined at a UNESCO-convened validation meeting, October 2024
position_end: Draft validated at a UNESCO workshop; no tabling, passage or gazettal on file

subject: gov.legislate
name: ARN sector regulations (Decrees 14, 15 and 16 of 2010)
milestone: Gazetted in the 2.o Suplemento to Boletim Oficial n.o 38, 22 September 2010
position_end: In force since 2010: supervision, sanctions and dispute resolution (14/2010), public-consultation procedure (15/2010) and the provision of communications networks and services (16/2010)
note: The public-consultation procedure is the instrument the ARN used for the 2026 electronic-transactions bill.

subject: gov.legislate
name: Digital Integrity (Dissemination of False Information on the Internet) Law
milestone: CNT (transitional parliament) unanimously passed, with amendments, the Law on the Dissemination of False Information on the Internet - framed by spokesman Fernando Vaz as targeting those who spread hate and act against the State; enforcement mechanisms, including for citizens abroad, left unstated
position_end: Enacted 21 May 2026 (CNT unanimous passage, with amendments); publication/in-force date and enforcement mechanisms unconfirmed; first invoked by the Ministry of Communication on 21 Jul 2026 over a false TikTok-shutdown claim
sources: 2026-05-23 Guinea-Bissau CNT passes Digital Integrity (online falsehoods) Law|2026-07-21-ang-ministerio-comunicacao-tiktok-desmentido

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Communications Law (revised)
status: Under review, Council of Ministers approved with amendments
milestone: Council of Ministers approved, with amendments, a proposed Electronic Communications Law replacing the outdated 2010 telecom regime, under the transitional presidency of Horta Inta-a; not confirmed passed by the CNT or published/in force
position_start: Did not exist - the 2010 Electronic Communications regime remained nominally in force
position_end: Council of Ministers approved a revised bill, with amendments; not yet confirmed passed by the CNT or in force

note: Event date is a year-precision proxy; exact Council of Ministers session date unconfirmed

subject: gov.legislate
name: Electronic Transactions Bill 2025
milestone: Put to public consultation by the ARN board under Aviso n.o 01/CA/ARN/2026, 8 May 2026
position_end: Revised draft published for public consultation by the ARN; no submission deadline, transmission to government or enactment date on file
note: The draft text itself carries a legislative-supplement header dated 6 September 2025.

subject: gov.legislate
name: ICT Framework Law (Lei n.o 5/2010)
milestone: Enacted by Lei n.o 5/2010 of 27 May 2010, Boletim Oficial n.o 21, 3.o Suplemento
position_end: In force since 2010; the base holds no amendment or replacement
note: The framework statute the sector’s later decrees and the ARN’s mandate rest on.

subject: gov.protect
name: National Data Governance and Protection Policy (decree)
milestone: Council of Ministers approved the draft decree (Politica Nacional de Governanca e Protecao de Dados) alongside decrees on interoperability and cybersecurity strategy; no confirmation on file of gazettal or entry into force
position_start: Draft decree approved by Council of Ministers 2025-07-10; not confirmed published or in force
position_end: Unchanged; no further movement on file
sources: 2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)

subject: gov.regional
name: AUDA-NEPAD Programme for African Developing Island Economies (Guinea-Bissau participation)
milestone: AUDA-NEPAD launched the Programme for African Developing Island Economies at the STC-TTIM Ministerial Segment in Abidjan, covering Guinea-Bissau among seven states; ministers adopted a communique committing to a 2026-2031 roadmap with six pillars including digital transformation
position_end: Ministerial communique adopted 24 Jul 2026 committing Guinea-Bissau to the Programme's 2026-2031 roadmap; no country-level implementation reported yet
note: Continental seven-state programme; Guinea-Bissau-specific national actions under it not yet reported

subject: gov.regional
name: CPLP digital rights charter
milestone: Signed at São Tomé by all nine member states, 19 July 2024
position_end: Expressly declaratory and non-binding, committing members to meaningful connectivity on non-discriminatory and affordable terms, personal data protection, cybersecurity cooperation, digital literacy and capacity building and non-fragmentation of the digital environment, and condemning blanket internet shutdowns; the first named activity in the Lusophone data-governance frame since is a Maputo workshop of 8-10 December 2025 at which UNESCO launched the Portuguese edition of its Data Governance Toolkit and more than 40 data-protection authorities and ICT regulators mapped national data ecosystems and governance gaps against the African Union Data Policy Framework and the Smart Africa Data Governance Blueprint
note: declaratory: no domestic measure is recorded as taken under it

subject: gov.regional
name: ECOWAS Supplementary Act on Personal Data Protection (A/SA.1/01/10)
milestone: Adopted by the ECOWAS Authority of Heads of State and Government, Abuja, 16 February 2010
position_end: In force as regional law since 2010; it is the applicable data-protection instrument while Guinea-Bissau has no domestic statute and no data-protection authority appointed
note: The absence of a domestic law and of an appointed authority is what makes the regional act load-bearing here.

subject: finance.new
name: MIGA guarantee - Sonatel/Orange Bissau S.A. equity investment
milestone: MIGA approved a US$25,435,357 guarantee (FY2025) to Sonatel SA covering its equity investment in Orange Bissau S.A., part of the combined Orange Guinea/Guinea-Bissau programme
position_start: Guarantee active, in force; US$0 disbursed (as captured)
position_end: Same - no new disbursement or status update found within the window
note: Part of combined Orange Guinea/Guinea-Bissau programme, EUR433.7m total across three tranches (PIDs 14394/14395/15192), approved 2023-08-12

subject: finance.new
name: UNDP Mais Digit@l for Guinea-Bissau grant
milestone: UNDP committed a US$3,360,500 grant (IATI OUTPUT 01004393) for a national digital-transformation programme implementing ENTD.GW with UNU-EGOV technical assistance
position_start: Active grant; early-stage disbursement of US$566,152 of US$3,360,500 recorded
position_end: Same - no newer disbursement figure held within the window
note: Commit-USD taken as total programme budget (2025-2030) per spec guidance; IATI record shows only the early $566K disbursement

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank WARDIP-GB (DTfA/WARDIP SOP1) IDA grant
milestone: WARDIP-GB programme launch ceremony presided by President Embalo in Bissau, marking the start of in-country implementation of the World Bank-financed grant
position_start: Implementation under way following the April 2025 launch; national fibre-backbone design (2,877 km, 56 nodes) published, private-sector wholesale-telecom partner not yet selected
position_end: Same - no new status-fixing milestone found within the window; backbone procurement stage unchanged as far as the base holds

subject: infra.connect
name: .GW country-code top-level domain
milestone: Internationalised domain names supported from 2026-06-05
position_start: Registration in unaccented Latin characters only
position_end: The national registry implemented support for internationalised domain names in the .GW top-level domain, allowing registration of addresses using the accented characters of Portuguese and of other languages used in the country
note: announced by the national regulator through the registry; no registration count or fee change is stated

subject: infra.connect
name: ACE (Africa Coast to Europe) submarine cable landing
milestone: Guinea-Bissau connects to its first international submarine fibre-optic cable (ACE)
position_start: Live since March 2023; sole international connectivity link, national backbone still absent
position_end: Unchanged; still the sole international submarine link, WARDIP-GB national backbone not yet operational
sources: 2025-08-29 Fibre-optic deployment - Guinea-Bissau wants to learn from Chad
note: ACE landing date is background context in a 2025-08-29 secondary mention; no dedicated primary on the ACE connection event itself is held

subject: infra.connect
name: ECOWAS second submarine cable (Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea-Bissau)
milestone: Feasibility study reviewed and approved at the ECOWAS expert workshop, Monrovia, 22-24 October 2025
position_end: Member-state experts with technical and financial partners reviewed and approved the feasibility study for a second submarine cable serving Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau at a workshop organised by the ECOWAS Project Preparation and Development Unit in Monrovia, 22-24 October 2025; no route, cost, landing site or construction date is published
note: A regional project ECOWAS runs for four member states; the same record sits on the Cabo Verde, Liberia and Sierra Leone ledgers. Whether it is the same project as any nationally announced second landing is not stated by the source.

subject: infra.connect
name: RNEP-GB / WARDIP-GB Final Report (Apr 2025)
status: Not held, searched 2026-08-27 - the RNEP-GB final report is held and is a different document
position_end: Not held
note: The document posted at wardip.gw as the RNEP-GB final report is now held and is the National Research and Education Network study, not the WARDIP-GB backbone design; the backbone specifics (2,877 km, 56 nodes) still rest on an undated project-website primary.

subject: infra.connect
name: Starlink satellite internet service
milestone: Commercial launch
position_start: Commercially live since 2025-06-19, Guinea-Bissau's 7th West African / 20th continental Starlink market
position_end: Commercially live, unchanged; no newer status update on file
sources: 2025-04-10 ARN-TIC grants Starlink Guinea-Bissau provisional authorization|2025-06-19 Starlink enters Guinea-Bissau
note: An initial Dec 2024 provisional licence referenced in the June 2025 source is not itself held as a primary

subject: infra.connect
name: WARDIP-GB National Fibre-Optic Backbone
milestone: EIASS environmental and social safeguards study published, moving toward implementation
position_start: WARDIP programme launched (five components); no fixed backbone design published yet; Guinea-Bissau still lacked a national backbone and was seeking deployment experience from Chad (Aug 2025)
position_end: 2,877 km design specified (56 nodes, 4 phases, >99% population coverage target, private wholesale operator under exclusive licence); EIASS safeguards study published, project moving toward implementation procurement, not yet built
sources: 2025-04-02 President Embalo launches WARDIP in Guinea-Bissau|2025-08-29 Fibre-optic deployment - Guinea-Bissau wants to learn from Chad|2026-01-01 Guinea-Bissau National Fibre-Optic Backbone specifications (WARDIP-GB)|2026-05-21 WARDIP-GB fibre backbone environmental and social impact study (EIASS)
note: Backbone-spec source is an undated primary (date_source proxy, year precision), corroborated by the dated EIASS report

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency
milestone: Government presented WARDIP/NRD Cyber Security feasibility study results and committed to create a National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency (Minister Marciano Silva Barbeiro), framed as central to digital sovereignty and data protection
position_start: Announced and committed to (Jan 2025); not yet established
position_end: Still at commitment stage; no source confirms the Agency has been formally established or made operational
sources: 2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency
note: Distinct from the National Cybersecurity Strategy decree of July 2025; no subsequent source confirms establishment

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National Cybersecurity Strategy (decree)
milestone: Council of Ministers approved the draft decree for a National Cybersecurity Strategy, following the January 2025 WARDIP/NRD Cyber Security feasibility study; no confirmation on file of gazettal or entry into force
position_start: Draft decree approved by Council of Ministers 2025-07-10; not confirmed published or in force
position_end: Unchanged; no further movement on file
sources: 2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)|2025-01-22 Guinea-Bissau presents cybersecurity study, plans National Cybersecurity and Data Protection Agency

subject: dpi.exchange
name: ASYCUDAWorld customs management system
milestone: Went live across the customs estate, reported by UNCTAD 26 January 2026
position_end: Live at the Port of Bissau, Bissau International Airport and the customs offices of Sao Domingos, Gabu and Bafata, retiring the ASYCUDA++ installation

subject: dpi.exchange
name: eGIF-GW interoperability framework and platform
milestone: Version 2.0 of the framework, platform and enterprise architecture delivered under WARDIP-GB, July 2024
position_end: Framework, interoperability platform and enterprise architecture specified at version 2.0 under WARDIP-GB; the base holds no record of the platform entering service
note: The technical framework, distinct from the interoperability regulation approved in 2026 and recorded separately.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Interoperability Regulation (public/private digital systems and platforms)
milestone: Government approval of the national interoperability regulation, announced 2026-08-08 by the WARDIP programme in Guinea-Bissau
position_start: Council of Ministers approval of the draft decree (2025-07-10); no later update on promulgation or publication found
position_end: Approved by the government as a national interoperability framework, presented as Guinea-Bissau's contribution to WARDIP; the announcing record names no decree number, gazettal or entry-into-force date
sources: 2026-08-08-guineabissau-national-interoperability-framework|2025-07-10 Guinea-Bissau Council of Ministers approves three digital decrees (interoperability, data governance, cybersecurity)
note: Approval is reported by the World Bank-backed programme that supports the work, not by a gazette; the paired data-governance and cybersecurity decrees approved the same day in 2025 are recorded separately under Governance and regulation and have not moved

subject: dpi.id
name: ENBIC (ECOWAS biometric ID) - Guinea-Bissau deployment
milestone: 262 women cross-border traders receive ENBIC cards in Sao Domingos (Cacheu) under a Guinea-Bissau-Senegal women-traders mobility pilot run by the National Borders Commission, ECOWAS-backed and GIZ-financed
position_start: Operationalized nationally (Guinea-Bissau one of six ECOWAS states to fully operationalize ENBIC); no field-level distribution reported (2025-06)
position_end: Operationalized, plus a first reported field-issuance pilot - 262 ENBIC cards issued to women cross-border traders in Sao Domingos, March 2026, under a Guinea-Bissau-Senegal mobility project
sources: 2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems|2026-03-16 Women traders receive ECOWAS biometric ID in Sao Domingos, Guinea-Bissau
note: Movement reflects a field-issuance pilot within an already-Implemented status, not a status-tier change

subject: dpi.id
name: PASSE automated border entry and exit control system
milestone: Launched at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport, 22-23 January 2025
position_end: In service at Osvaldo Vieira International Airport: automated searching and a register of entry and exit movements, ceded by Portugal’s Sistema de Seguranca Interna and adapted locally under the EU-funded GESTDOC project
note: Launched at the same event that closed GESTDOC and launched SIREC, recorded separately.

subject: dpi.id
name: Semlex biometric national-ID production network
milestone: Semlex opens a production centre in Safim (Biombo) - the third in Biombo, 100 cards per day - bringing the national network to 18 biometric-ID production centres; further centres planned for Sao Domingos and Bolama (Bijagos)
position_start: Functional biometric national-ID card system in place nationally; decentralisation network not itemised (2025-06)
position_end: 18 production centres nationwide, including the newly opened Safim centre (Biombo, 100 cards/day, third in Biombo); further centres planned for Sao Domingos and Bolama (Bijagos) (2026-02)
sources: 2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems|2026-02-11 Semlex Guinea-Bissau strengthens access to biometric identification

subject: dpi.pay
name: Blockchain public wage-bill and pensions platform
milestone: Launched May 2024 under the IMF Extended Credit Facility
position_end: In service since May 2024, running eligibility, budgeting, payment approval and disbursement of civil-service salaries and pensions on a tamper-evident ledger with near-real-time discrepancy alerts; built over four years with Ernst & Young as technical adviser
note: Coverage figures quoted for November 2024 were a stated expectation at the time of writing and are not confirmed in this base.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic-money active accounts (UEMOA/BCEAO reporting)
milestone: BCEAO's 2024 UEMOA digital-financial-services annual report (published January 2026) records Guinea-Bissau's e-money active accounts up 33.28% in 2024 - the union's second-highest growth rate after Togo's 76.87%
position_end: Active e-money accounts up 33.28% in 2024; Guinea-Bissau holds 1.94% of UEMOA accounts opened, about 0.7%/1% of regional transaction volume/value, via 2 e-money issuing initiatives nationally (of 69 across the union)
note: Data year is 2024 (report dated January 2026); figures are Guinea-Bissau's shares within a regional report, not a standalone national release

subject: dpi.pay
name: KONTAKTU simplified tax and contribution payment system
milestone: Payment guidance issued by the Direccao-Geral das Contribuicoes e Impostos, 24 March 2021
position_end: In service since 2021 for simplified payment of contributions, taxes and fees; no later update on file

subject: dpi.pay
name: PI-SPI authorised participants
milestone: BCEAO participant list, update of 31 July 2026
position_start: Three participants when PI-SPI opened to the public on 30 September 2025
position_end: Five institutions authorised to open PI-SPI instant-payment services to the public - Banco da Africa Ocidental, BDU, Coris Bank, Ecobank and Orabank - out of 104 participants across the eight WAEMU states
note: Guinea-Bissau and Niger hold the joint-smallest national counts on the union list.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Treasury Single Account (CUT) Regulation
milestone: Regulation approved, announced by the Ministry of Economy and Finance 18 March 2025
position_end: Approved: a central Treasury account through which all state fiscal and non-fiscal receipts are centralised and expenditure operations made; no entry-into-force date on file

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth-registration rate (under-fives)
milestone: Birth registration among under-fives rises to 46% (from an undated 23.4% baseline) via a UNICEF/Ministry of Public Health partnership; target is at least 90% via digitization
position_end: Same - no fresher measurement found; overall birth registration remains below 50%
sources: 2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems|2025-06-01 Guinea-Bissau to digitize civil identification, registry and notary services

subject: dpi.registry
name: Electoral register update and card replacement
milestone: Register handed to the elections commission 2026-08-18 for the 30 August referendum
position_end: The updated electoral register handed to the elections commission in both physical and electronic form, recording 966,152 registered voters, unchanged from the last update, alongside 25,146 replacement voter cards issued in a 30-day nationwide operation from 13 July to 11 August 2026 by 51 brigades covering every region
note: the electorate figure is unchanged from the previous update, so the operation replaced cards rather than adding registrants; no audit or de-duplication statement is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: SIREC (Integrated System of Citizen Registers and Statistics)
milestone: Ministry of Justice Civil Registration Office (Raul Gomes) describes SIREC digitizing births, deaths and marriages, with UNDP-trained officers, roughly three months into rollout; birth registration remains below 50% (~46% of under-fives)
position_start: Rollout under way since approximately March 2025 (Bissau-first); birth registration around 46% of under-fives, still below 50% overall
position_end: Same as start - no fresher status update found; birth registration still cited at 46% (last measured 2025-06), no dated confirmation of regional extension
sources: 2025-06-10 Guinea-Bissau deploys efforts to digitize birth registration, national ID systems|2025-06-01 Guinea-Bissau to digitize civil identification, registry and notary services
note: Since date is inferred (~3 months before the 2025-06-10 interview)

subject: dpi.registry
name: UNDP Building National ID project (civil-registry books scanning and digitization)
milestone: UNDP project, co-financed by the Swiss Confederation, sets up a digitization centre and develops software to recover and digitize paper civil-registry books (births, deaths, marriages, annotations) as the country's main national identity platform
position_start: Digitization centre established; software development to scan and recover paper registry books under way (2024, year-precision baseline)
position_end: Same - no dated update found since 2024
sources: 2024-01-01 Building a National Identification System - Scanning and Digitizing the Civil Registry Books in Guinea-Bissau
note: date_source is proxy; year precision only

subject: dpi.govtech
name: SIIC (Integrated Criminal Information System)
milestone: Reformulated centre inaugurated by the Minister of Justice, 9 March 2023
position_end: In service at the Judicial Police since the reformulated centre opened in March 2023; no later update on file

subject: capacity.training
name: STARTOCODE digital-skills programme (Telecel + Government)
milestone: Joint decree signed creating the STARTOCODE Coordination and Monitoring Committee, formalising programme implementation
position_end: Coordination committee stood up to supervise annual training of 1,000 youth over four years in programming, data analysis and cloud computing, with emphasis on women and people with disabilities
sources: 2026-05-07 Telecel and Guinea-Bissau Government launch STARTOCODE Coordination Committee
note: Company press release (pr-wire flag)

subject: capacity.research
name: RNEP-GB (National Research and Education Network)
milestone: Proposed in the WARDIP-GB final report, July 2024
position_end: Proposed only: a three-phase roadmap from legal establishment and pilot to national reach, serving 32 higher-education institutions and joining WACREN; nothing on record being built
note: The consultancy study arrived in the base two years after its stated month; it is a reference design, not a delivery.

note: The regulator’s own measure of mobile stations, not a measure of internet use.

subject: data.statistics

milestone: National Summary Data Page launched, announced by the IMF 8 July 2024
position_end: Publishing essential macroeconomic data under the IMF’s enhanced General Data Dissemination System

name: National Statistical System Framework Law (Lei n.o 6/2007)
milestone: Enacted by Lei n.o 6/2007 of 10 September 2007
position_end: In force since 2007, as amended by Decreto n.o 4/2023 and Decreto-Lei n.o 2/2023
note: The statutory base for the INE and for the census and vital-statistics work recorded separately.

position_end: Preliminary results released 2026-07-23 - population 2,191,202, 50.7% women, 45.7% urban, 304,939 households, 559,303 dwellings; leaves a digital-cartography and technology base for future operations; full tabulations pending
